answers.answer: In a four-player game, select 3 randomly chosen Escape Pod tokens. Place the lowest-numbered pod in Section A, the next in B, then alternate A/B; all begin with the Locked side up. Put 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, plus 1 additional Adult per player (so 7 Adults for four players) in the Intruder bag.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 7 and 10: “3 for 3–4 players”; lowest-numbered A, next B, alternate; all “Locked”; bag tokens listed.

answers.answer: 1. Remove Corporate and Personal Objective cards showing a player count above the actual player count. 2. Shuffle the two decks separately and deal each player one of each, kept hidden, before the Character draft. 3. On the first Encounter—when the first Intruder miniature appears, of any type—each player chooses one of their two Objectives and removes the other face down from the game without looking at it; players may not look at other players’ removed Objectives. 4. Eggs do not trigger this choice because Eggs are not Intruders.
answers.evidence: Setup step 16; Critical gameplay moments: “first time an Intruder miniature ... appears”; Eggs are not Intruders.

answers.answer: Discard the Action card being played and two additional Action cards to pay its printed cost of 2. The two Contamination cards cannot pay any Action cost and remain in hand. If the Action card has two sections separated by OR, choose one section to use.
answers.evidence: Actions from Action cards: discard the card and required additional cards; “If a card has two sections ... ‘OR,’ choose one”; Action Cost says Contamination cards can never be discarded to pay.

answers.answer: 1. The Character takes 1 Light Wound after finishing their own round, including when that round ends by passing. 2. Once passed, they cannot take further normal Actions this Player Phase (Interruption is the stated exception). 3. When passing, they may discard any number of cards from their hand. 4. Later players’ rounds do not make this Character take Fire damage again; the Fire wound is assessed at the end of that Character’s own round.
answers.evidence: Player Phase rules: a Character ending their round in Fire suffers 1 Light Wound; after passing no further normal Actions; “When passing, you may discard any number of cards.”

answers.answer: 1. On entry, flip the unexplored Room tile face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token. 2. Rotate the tile so the token’s Item number faces the board’s Item Counter symbol (except the Nest and Room Covered in Slime); resolve the token effect, then remove the token to the box. 3. Silence suppresses the Noise roll; if the Character has Slime, resolve Danger instead. Danger also suppresses the roll and moves all eligible neighboring Intruders into the Room; if none are eligible, place Noise in every connected Corridor that lacks one, counting Technical Corridors if there is an Entrance. 4. If the destination already contains any Character or Intruder, do not roll for Noise. Otherwise, after exploration/effect resolution, roll Noise. An Exploration Danger result substitutes its own resolution for that roll.
answers.evidence: Movement, Rooms, and Corridors; Exploration tokens; Noise roll: exploration and token are resolved on first entry, with Silence/Danger and occupancy exceptions.

answers.answer: Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards. It follows normal Movement restrictions and replaces the Noise roll after moving with placing a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the destination; FAQ clarification says it also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results. It is forbidden in Combat and when all destination Corridors already contain Noise. A Closed Door blocks movement, and a miniature cannot stop in a Corridor.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions: Careful Movement costs 2, replaces noise with chosen marker, and is unavailable in Combat; Closed Doors block; Corridors cannot be occupied as stops.

answers.answer: 1. Because the indicated Corridor already has Noise, resolve an Encounter. First discard all Noise markers from Corridors connected to the Room, including the shared Technical Corridors space if the Room has an Entrance. 2. Draw one Intruder token and place its matching miniature in the Room. Keep the drawn non-Blank token aside outside the bag until a rule returns it. 3. Compare its number with the triggering player’s hand, counting Action and Contamination cards; fewer cards than the number causes a Surprise Attack against that Character, otherwise nothing happens. If it is Blank, there is no miniature: restore Noise in each connected Corridor and return the Blank to the bag. Contamination cards count in the comparison.
answers.evidence: Encounter sequence and Player Reference combat quick reference: discard all connected Noise, draw/place, compare triggering hand including Contamination, set non-Blank token aside.

answers.answer: Danger moves all eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into the destination, provided they are not in Combat with any Character. If there are no eligible Intruders, put a Noise marker in every connected Corridor lacking one (counting Technical Corridors when applicable). Intruders moving into a Character’s Room do not create an Encounter; they are simply in Combat. Slime turns a Silence result into Danger.
answers.evidence: Exploration tokens and Noise roll: “move ALL eligible Intruders”; none means place markers; an Intruder merely moving into a Room with a Character is NOT an Encounter; Slime changes Silence to Danger.

answers.answer: In an Encounter, a Blank produces no Intruder miniature; put a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to the Room. If it was the last token in the bag, add 1 Adult token if one is available, then return the Blank to the bag. By contrast, when Blank is drawn during Intruder bag development, add 1 Adult token if available and return the Blank; that rule does not restore connected Noise.
answers.evidence: Encounters: Blank restores connected Noise and adds Adult only if it was the last bag token; Event Phase bag development: Blank adds an Adult if available and returns.

answers.answer: Both Intruders stay in their original Room. They simultaneously destroy the Closed Door token. A Destroyed Door cannot later be Closed again, except by the Plasma Torch Item. An Intruder appearing because of a Noise roll comes through a Closed Door regardless of the Door, so the appearance is not blocked.
answers.evidence: Door tokens: multiple Intruders moving from the same Room destroy the Door simultaneously and all stay; destroyed Doors cannot be Closed again except Plasma Torch; Noise appearance ignores a Closed Door.

answers.answer: The Intruder disappears into the ducts: remove its miniature, discard all its Injury markers, and return its token to the Intruder bag. The Noise marker already on the Technical Corridors space remains. Characters normally cannot use Technical Corridors, with exceptions for the Mechanic’s Technical Corridors Action card and the Technical Corridor Plans Item; Door tokens can never be placed there.
answers.evidence: Technical Corridors: entering Intruder returns to bag with injuries discarded; Noise marker is not removed; only specified Character exceptions; Doors cannot be placed there.

answers.answer: 1. Each ordinary Shoot or Melee Action costs 1 Action card. Shoot requires a Weapon in Hand with Ammo: choose one Intruder in your Room, discard 1 Ammo, roll the Combat die, and apply a hit’s Injury. A blank misses; the two-hit result inflicts 2 Injuries when Shooting, before Weapon modifications. 2. For Melee, draw 1 Contamination card onto your Action discard pile, choose one Intruder in your Room, and roll. A miss also gives the Character 1 Serious Wound; a two-hit result counts as only 1 Injury in Melee.
answers.evidence: Combat: Shoot (cost 1) and Melee Attack (cost 1) procedures, including Ammo, Contamination, miss penalty, and treatment of two-hit die result.

answers.answer: After damage, place Injury markers on the Intruder and check its Injury Effect. A Larva dies at 1 Injury and is removed; an Adult is checked by drawing 1 Intruder Attack card and comparing its blood value to its injuries (blood value equal to or below injuries means death); a Queen is checked by drawing 2 cards and adding their blood values. On death, place an Intruder Carcass in the Room for any dead Intruder except a Larva (the Egg is likewise removed when killed at 1 Injury). If either card in a Queen’s check shows a Retreat arrow, it retreats instead of using a numerical death result: draw an Event card and move it through the Corridor number in that card’s Intruder movement section, then discard the Event card.
answers.evidence: Combat, Intruder Injuries and death; Intruder Retreat: Larva/Egg 1 injury, Adult one blood check, Queen two summed checks, Carcass except Larvae, retreat overrides check.

answers.answer: Before moving, resolve one Intruder Attack for each of the two Intruders, starting with the larger type. The target of Escape attacks is the escaping Character. If the Character dies, their Corpse remains in the Room they tried to leave. If they survive, complete movement to the neighboring Room; since it is empty, roll Noise, and because it is unexplored, explore it normally. The Escape Action costs 1 Action card.
answers.evidence: Character Escape: one separate attack per Intruder before movement, larger first; death leaves Corpse in source Room; survival completes move and destination exploration/Noise.

answers.answer: With several Characters in the Room, the Intruder targets the one whose player has the fewest Action cards in hand; on a tie, use the Character with the First Player token or next in turn order. Draw one Intruder Attack card: a matching Intruder symbol is a hit and resolves its effect; otherwise it misses, and the blood icon is ignored. A Larva does not draw an Attack card: remove its miniature and place it on the target’s Character board, and the target gains 1 Contamination card. If the target already has a Larva, the attacking Larva disappears, the existing Larva stays, and the Character still gains the Contamination card without automatically dying. Put that Contamination on top of the target’s Action discard pile.
answers.evidence: Intruder Attack and Infest (Larva attack); Contamination cards: a gained card is placed atop Action discard pile.

answers.answer: Dressing one of three Serious Wounds does not prevent death from another Wound: dressing ignores that card’s effect but it still counts toward the three-wound limit. A third Light Wound clears the Light Wound track and becomes a Serious Wound; with three Serious Wounds already, any further Wound kills the Character. Heal removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound card, as specified by the healing effect. On death, place a Character Corpse token in the Room as an Object and drop all Heavy Objects there; Item cards disappear from the game.
answers.evidence: Character Wounds and death; FAQ: dressing does not prevent death at 3 Serious Wounds; death drops Heavy Objects and Item cards disappear.

answers.answer: 1. Canteen and Shower scan only Contamination cards in the Character’s hand, removing all non-Infected cards; an Infected result places a Larva on the board (if a Larva is already there, the Character dies and a Creeper appears in the Room). 2. Surgery scans all Contamination cards in deck, hand, and discard, removes all Infected cards from the game, and removes a Larva from the board if present. It then gives 1 Light Wound, automatically passes, and shuffles all cards—including the entire hand and remaining Contamination cards—into the Action deck, leaving the hand empty until next turn.
answers.evidence: Player Reference Room Actions: Canteen/Shower hand-only scan; Surgery scans all zones, removes infected and Larva, wounds, passes and shuffles all cards.

answers.answer: 1. In a Room with uncarried Eggs, Shoot or Melee them; each Injury destroys one Egg. A missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor a Wound. A successful Egg Melee’s Contamination handling is explicitly unresolved by the summary’s source limitation. 2. Grenades destroy 2 Eggs and Molotov Cocktails destroy 1; they may be thrown at a Room with uncarried Eggs as if an Intruder were there. 3. Fire destroys 1 uncarried Egg in the Room during each Fire Damage step. 4. Make a Noise roll after every single attempt to destroy an Egg. 5. When no Eggs remain, the Nest is destroyed and marked with 1 Injury marker.
answers.evidence: Eggs and the Nest: methods, missed Egg Melee exception, Noise roll after each attempt, and Nest destruction; source limitation says successful Egg Melee Contamination is unresolved.

answers.answer: 1. Use the Evacuation Section A/B Room Action, paying 2 Action cards. The Pod must be Unlocked and have a free Character space in that Section. Roll Noise first; entry fails if an Intruder appears or is present in the Section Room, or if that Room has a Malfunction marker. Each Pod holds up to 2 Characters; Heavy Objects use no Character space. 2. After boarding, launch immediately or wait. A waiting occupant can, at the start of their first round in the next Player Phase, stay and pass, launch, or exit for free into the Section Room and take a full round of 2 Actions. Waiting occupants count as present for Noise rolls from bag development; if an Intruder appears in the Section Room while they wait, all pod occupants return to that Room. Another Character boarding a waiting Pod may launch immediately with them aboard. A later Malfunction does not affect an already boarded Character’s ability to wait, launch, or exit.
answers.evidence: Escape Pods and Room Actions: entry requirements, capacity, launch/wait/exit options, noise presence, Intruder return, and later Malfunction ruling.

answers.answer: 1. Victory Check order is Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, then Objectives. 2. If two or three Engines are Damaged, the ship explodes and everything aboard dies, including hibernating Characters and Intruders; launched Pod passengers are already away. 3. If the ship survives but is not headed to Earth, Characters asleep in the Hibernatorium die; the ship is not destroyed and Intruders do not die. Quarantine is the exception: its Character survives hibernation when the destination is Mars. 4. Each surviving Character, including pod passengers, undergoes the Contamination check. Scan Contamination cards in deck, discard, and hand. If any are Infected, shuffle all Action and Contamination cards from those zones and draw four; any Contamination card among those four kills the Character. A Larva on the board triggers the same shuffle-and-draw-four test directly, skipping the initial Scan.
answers.evidence: Victory Check: ordered checks; Engines and Coordinates; Contamination applies to “each surviving Character (hibernating or evacuated).”
